commit.subject: Merge main (through v0.0.66, incl. #399 body substitution) into sigv4 branch
commit.body:
Conflicts in http-proxy.ts, sandbox-manager.ts, and tls-terminate-proxy.ts
came from #399's body-substitution transform landing on main alongside this
branch's SigV4 re-signing. Resolved using the rehearsed composition from the
local integration branch (merge 323d763), which was built for exactly this
pairing:

- literal-hash collectBody reads through the body-substitution transform
  (bodyTransform ? body.pipe(bodyTransform) : body) so the recomputed
  payload hash and signature cover the substituted bytes, never the
  sentinel-bearing bytes the client wrote
- content-length is restored from the buffered substituted body
  (fwdHeaders['content-length'] = String(bufferedBody.length))
- three-way upstream pipe: buffered re-sign path sends the buffered body
  verbatim; otherwise transform-pipe when substitution applies; else bare
- over-cap fail-open drains via bodySource.resume() so the transform chain
  keeps flowing

Also brings over the integration branch's composition tests
(credential-mask-sigv4.test.ts: bodySubstitution option on makeStack plus
the "body substitution composes with SigV4 re-signing" suite).

Post-rehearsal main changes (#409 GRPC_PROXY CONNECT URL, v0.0.66 bump)
auto-merged cleanly and are unaffected by the resolutions.

No-Verification-Needed: merge-resolution reusing rehearsed, tested integration content; suite matches main baseline

commit.subject: Cap the body buffer for SigV4 literal-hash re-signing at 64 MiB
commit.body:
collectBody buffered the entire request body with no size limit, so one
large signed upload from the sandboxed process could pin arbitrary host
memory (awslabs/aws-sigv4-proxy has the same unbounded buffer; we fail
closed instead). Bodies over MAX_SIGV4_RESIGN_BODY_BYTES are denied with
the standard 403, the partial buffer is discarded, and the upstream
request is never constructed; the denial names the limit and points at
UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD, which streams without buffering.

The cap is injectable via createHttpProxyServer (test seam only, like
tlsTerminateUpstreamCA) so the over-cap path is testable without a
64 MiB fixture upload per test.

commit.subject: Close the presigned-policy bypass via a non-AWS Authorization header
commit.body:
detectSigv4 returned null whenever an Authorization header was present
but not classifiable as SigV4/SigV4A, without ever looking at the query
string. A sandboxed client could therefore attach a junk Authorization
value (e.g. Basic ...) to a presigned-style URL carrying a masked
credential and dodge the presigned deny policy entirely.

Fall through to the query-parameter check whenever the Authorization
header does not itself classify — including SigV4-shaped values with no
parsable Credential scope, which were the same bypass one byte away. A
classifiable header signature still wins over the query when both are
present, and unmasked presigned URLs remain untouched.
commit.author: elhajjj

commit.subject: Fix Bun stream corruption in the TLS-terminate relay (pull-mode reads)
commit.body:
Under Bun, the socket an http server delivers via its 'connect' event
corrupts its byte stream across the pause()/resume() cycles that pipe()
uses for flow control, once downstream writes queue. Through the
terminating proxy's client->inner relay this surfaced as the inner TLS
server failing record MAC verification mid-upload: curl exit 56 /
bad_record_mac, near-deterministic at 16 MiB (49/50 on Bun 1.3.14),
rare-but-real at the 256 KiB the at-cap CI test uploads (the
macos/arm64 flake this fixes). Node is unaffected.

Bisection: bare CONNECT tunnel + pipe reproduces it; the same relay
that never calls pause() is clean (0/160+ across 4-64 MiB, Bun
1.3.13/1.3.14, with and without CPU load). So relay the client socket
with paused-mode reads ('readable' + read()), which provide identical
backpressure without ever pausing a flowing stream.

Adds a 16 MiB literal-hash PUT regression test that fails single-shot
on the old relay and pins byte-intact delivery end to end.
